maps.name: Carrier Group
maps.executiveSummary: Deep-ocean naval battlefield built for fleet-scale warfare, carrier-based air operations, autonomous maritime coordination, and multi-domain combat across sea, air, and long-range missile envelopes. Features open ocean sectors, shifting waves, carrier decks, destroyer screens, submarine lanes, missile arcs, radar pickets, logistics ships, sensor-fusion under sea clutter and radar interference, comms-relay warfare, and logistics.

goals.name: Fleet-Scale Naval Warfare
goals.description: Coordinated fleets: carriers, destroyers, cruisers, submarines, drones, and aircraft. Engagements occur across massive distances.

goals.name: Carrier Air Wing Operations
goals.description: Fighters, bombers, VTOLs, and recon drones launch from carrier decks. Air superiority determines strike capability and fleet survival.

goals.name: Destroyer Screens & Missile Defense
goals.description: Destroyers and cruisers form layered defense rings using AA guns, CIWS, missile interceptors, and EW systems.

goals.name: Submarine Shadow Zones
goals.description: Submarines exploit deep-water lanes, thermal layers, and sonar shadows to ambush surface ships or disrupt logistics.

goals.name: Autonomous Maritime Routing
goals.description: Autonomous units choose routes based on wave patterns, radar clarity, sonar returns, missile arcs, and threat vectors.

goals.name: Sensor & Information Warfare
goals.description: Radar clutter, sea spray, thermal layers, jamming, and EW interference degrade sensors. Relay ships restore clarity; destroying relays creates blind pockets.

goals.name: Logistics & Resources
goals.description: Fuel ships, supply vessels, and repair barges serve as resupply nodes. Protecting logistics ships is critical.

maps.deployment: Fixed deployment budget ~10,000 points. Blue deploys from southwest carrier strike group; Red from northeast cruiser-led battle group.

maps.name: Blind Zone

goals.name: Information Manipulation & Deception
goals.description: EW drones, false-signal emitters, spoof beacons, and decoy units reshape the tactical landscape.

goals.name: Autonomous Counter-EW Routing
goals.description: Routes based on signal strength, interference pockets, terrain occlusion, and fallback relay availability; units adapt to misleading data.

goals.name: Dense-Terrain Combat
goals.description: Close-range engagements dominate; vegetation, rocks, and fog create stealth zones and unpredictable movement corridors.

goals.name: Logistics & Resources
goals.description: Fuel caches, bunker stations, and buried cable hubs serve as resupply nodes; convoys navigate blackout corridors.

goals.name: Autonomy & Behavior Testing
goals.description: Units choose routes based on cover density, elevation micro-changes, sensor clarity, and threat vectors; no environmental noise.

goals.name: Sensor & Information Warfare

goals.name: Logistics & Resources
